title: Worker accounts can read outsourced-worker PII and private documents
evidence: [.qa-audit/production-2026-10-04/http-evidence.json](<C:/Users/JARVIS/Desktop/Al Jazeera CRM/.qa-audit/production-2026-10-04/http-evidence.json>); [.qa-audit/production-2026-10-04/deep-evidence.json](<C:/Users/JARVIS/Desktop/Al Jazeera CRM/.qa-audit/production-2026-10-04/deep-evidence.json>). Worker list/detail returned 200. File route returned 200 and synthetic private bytes through the real auth/controller/service chain; only the external CDN fetch was stubbed.
problem: The client hides this section using employeeCreate, but these backend reads have authentication only. Neither a read permission nor record visibility is applied. The raw list limit also accepts 1,000,000 and returned all 1,201 synthetic records.
impact: Security: high confidentiality impact. Business: personnel/identity data exposure. Users: all outsourced workers in this collection. Likelihood: high with any Worker account. Exploitability: direct API request, no elevated role. Production: release blocker if this code is deployed.
repro: Log in as the disposable Worker. GET the collection and a seeded record ID, then its document file endpoint. Run http-tests.mjs and deep-tests.mjs against the isolated runtime. Do not repeat against real personnel records.

title: Forced password change is enforced only by the UI
evidence: [.qa-audit/production-2026-10-04/latest-regressions.json](<C:/Users/JARVIS/Desktop/Al Jazeera CRM/.qa-audit/production-2026-10-04/latest-regressions.json>): weak-password login returned forcePasswordChange:true; its bearer token still fetched /api/me/profile with 200.
problem: Authentication loads the user but does not restrict a forcePasswordChange session. Closing/bypassing the frontend flow is unnecessary: the API token already works.
impact: Security: password-remediation control bypass. Business/users: account remains usable with a credential the system says must change. Likelihood: medium, conditional on a flagged account. Exploitability: direct authenticated request; this does not grant a higher role.
repro: Use a disposable flagged/weak-password account, POST /api/auth/login, then GET /api/me/profile using the returned token without changing its password. See latest-regressions.mjs.
fix: Issue a restricted password-change session or reject normal protected endpoints while the flag is set. Explicitly allow password change and logout, and return a stable machine-readable code that the UI handles.
test: YES — flagged token cannot access normal resources; password change clears the restriction; logout still works; ordinary users remain unaffected.

title: A joint coordinator can list a deployment but cannot open it
evidence: [.qa-audit/production-2026-10-04/final-probes.json](<C:/Users/JARVIS/Desktop/Al Jazeera CRM/.qa-audit/production-2026-10-04/final-probes.json>): confirmed joint CoordinatorB saw the deployment in a 200 list response, then received 403 on detail.
problem: List visibility follows mobilisation coordinators; detail visibility for an Employee worker follows the employee current coordinator. These are different policies for the same deployment.
impact: Security: no new unauthorized disclosure demonstrated beyond the intended list membership. Business/users: legitimate joint coordinator blocked. Likelihood: high for shared mobilisations. Exploitability: normal navigation. Production: workflow interruption.
repro: Create a mobilisation for CoordinatorA’s worker; add CoordinatorB as a confirmed joint coordinator; grant needed section access. List as B, then request the returned deployment ID. See final-probes.mjs.
fix: Define deployment visibility once using the intended mobilisation/worker policy and call it from list, detail, hours, invoices and downloads. Preserve stricter mutation permissions separately.
test: YES — both confirmed participants can perform intended reads; unrelated coordinator is excluded from list and detail; stale/removed membership is rejected.

title: Partial employee edits silently clear additional-document metadata
evidence: [.qa-audit/production-2026-10-04/latest-regressions.json](<C:/Users/JARVIS/Desktop/Al Jazeera CRM/.qa-audit/production-2026-10-04/latest-regressions.json>): updating only department returned additionalDocuments:[]. Rechecked the latest on-disk schema on October 5: parse({department:'Audit'}) also emitted additionalDocuments:[].
problem: The shared schema applies default([]) to additionalDocuments. Deriving the PATCH schema with partial() still materializes that default under the installed Zod version. The service writes the resulting empty array.
impact: Security: integrity rather than access-control issue. Business: document-register metadata loss. Users: any employee edited through a partial payload. Likelihood: high in normal partial updates. Exploitability: ordinary authorized PATCH. Production: release blocker; binary file deletion was not demonstrated.
repro: Seed an employee with one additional document. PATCH only {"department":"QA department"}. Read the employee and compare the array. latest-regressions.mjs records the HTTP proof.
fix: Remove create defaults from the shared PATCH object. Apply defaults only in create-specific schema/service and make updates preserve omitted keys. Review sibling optional defaults before changing them.
test: YES — omitted documents survive PATCH; explicit [] clears only when requested; creation still gets the intended default; nested omitted fields are retained.

title: Settlement overrides can persist Infinity as financial amounts
evidence: [.qa-audit/production-2026-10-04/latest-regressions.json](<C:/Users/JARVIS/Desktop/Al Jazeera CRM/.qa-audit/production-2026-10-04/latest-regressions.json>): overrideEosbGross:1e308 returned 201 with null monetary values in JSON; direct database check showed non-finite eosbGross and totalSettlement.
problem: An input may be finite while rounding by multiplying it by 100 overflows. The override has a minimum but no business maximum; computed values are persisted without a finite-value invariant.
impact: Security: integrity risk to an authorized financial workflow. Business: corrupted settlement totals/PDF/report inputs. Users: settlement operators and employees. Likelihood: low accidentally, easy with a crafted authorized request. Production: release blocker.
repro: POST /api/eosb for a disposable eligible employee with exitDate:2026-09-30, exitReason:EndOfContract, overrideEosbGross:1e308. Inspect both response and stored finite checks. See latest-regressions.mjs.
fix: Set realistic monetary/day bounds; validate every computed amount with Number.isFinite before persistence; use a consistent decimal or bounded minor-unit representation. Reject invalid results with 400/422 rather than storing them.
test: YES — extreme finite values are rejected with no write; boundaries and normal rounding pass; all saved settlement amounts are finite.

title: Concurrent final-settlement creation stores duplicates
evidence: [.qa-audit/production-2026-10-04/latest-regressions.json](<C:/Users/JARVIS/Desktop/Al Jazeera CRM/.qa-audit/production-2026-10-04/latest-regressions.json>): five concurrent EndOfContract requests returned five 201 responses; five settlements existed for one employee.
problem: The existing-record check and insertion are separate operations without a database uniqueness invariant. Latest edits exclude CurrentEmployee simulations from the lookup, but do not remove the final-settlement race.
impact: Security: data-integrity issue for authorized callers. Business: duplicate liabilities/review work, not proof of duplicate cash payout. Users: HR/accounts. Likelihood: medium with retries/double-submit. Exploitability: simultaneous authorized requests.
repro: Send five parallel identical final-settlement requests for one fresh employee. Count stored final settlements. See latest-regressions.mjs.
fix: Agree the final-settlement identity (employee plus employment episode if rehiring is supported). Enforce it with a suitable partial unique index that excludes CurrentEmployee simulations, plus idempotency and 409 handling. Reconcile existing duplicates before adding the index.
test: YES — concurrency stores exactly one final settlement; retried idempotency key returns the same result; simulations remain allowed; distinct employment episodes follow policy.

title: Leave-type PATCH permits a Sick policy that crashes submissions
evidence: [.qa-audit/production-2026-10-04/workflow-evidence.json](<C:/Users/JARVIS/Desktop/Al Jazeera CRM/.qa-audit/production-2026-10-04/workflow-evidence.json>): changing Manual to Sick without tiers returned 200; a subsequent Worker request returned 500.
problem: Create validation requires sickPayTiers, but update validation does not validate the merged policy’s cross-field invariant. Submission assumes tiers are present.
impact: Security: no access bypass. Business: broken policy prevents leave requests. Users: employees assigned that type. Likelihood: medium during policy edits. Exploitability: authorized administrator misconfiguration.
repro: Create Manual leave type; PATCH {"recurrence":"Sick"}; submit leave using its ID. See workflows.mjs.
fix: Merge stored policy with the patch, validate the complete policy using shared refinements, then persist. Reject invalid transitions and protect calculation code from malformed historic policies.

title: Leave entitlement combines requests from different future years
evidence: [.qa-audit/production-2026-10-04/deep-evidence.json](<C:/Users/JARVIS/Desktop/Al Jazeera CRM/.qa-audit/production-2026-10-04/deep-evidence.json>): a two-day annual allowance auto-approved June 2027; June 2028 then saw usedDays:2 and remainingDays:0 from the same 2026-based window.
problem: Eligibility uses the current service-year start and a lower-bound-only date filter. Future requests from different entitlement periods are pooled together.
impact: Security: entitlement integrity. Business/users: wrong automatic approval/review decisions and balances. Likelihood: medium when advance leave is allowed. Exploitability: ordinary request dates. Production: incorrect HR workflow.
repro: Create Annual policy with daysPerYear:2. Submit two days in June 2027, then two days in June 2028 for the same employee. See deep-tests.mjs.
fix: Define the entitlement period relative to the requested leave and bound both ends. Specify handling of cross-period leave and future booking limits. Preserve decision snapshots, while recomputing a fresh eligibility assessment for new requests.
test: YES — requests in separate service years do not consume each other; same-period requests do; anniversary and cross-period requests follow explicit policy.

title: A single calendar day can consume two leave days
evidence: [.qa-audit/production-2026-10-04/input-probes.json](<C:/Users/JARVIS/Desktop/Al Jazeera CRM/.qa-audit/production-2026-10-04/input-probes.json>): start 2026-10-25T06:00Z and end 2026-10-25T20:30Z returned days:2. Both timestamps fall on October 25 in UTC and Riyadh.
problem: Schemas accept timestamps but duration rounds elapsed fractional days before adding one. Calendar-day leave and elapsed-time arithmetic are mixed.
impact: Security: entitlement integrity. Business: incorrect leave balances. Users: API/mobile clients providing timestamps. Likelihood: medium. Exploitability: ordinary accepted input, no extra privilege.
repro: Submit the two timestamps above for a Manual leave type. Inspect days. See input-probes.mjs.
fix: Require date-only inputs or normalize both dates to the chosen business calendar before inclusive day counting. Use one documented date convention across API and UI.
test: YES — same-day times always count one; adjacent calendar dates count two; leap day, DST-independent business timezone and year boundaries pass.

title: Oversized JSON is reported as an internal server error
component: POST /api/auth/login with JSON exceeding the configured body limit
evidence: [.qa-audit/production-2026-10-04/input-probes.json](<C:/Users/JARVIS/Desktop/Al Jazeera CRM/.qa-audit/production-2026-10-04/input-probes.json>): an oversized body returned generic 500 rather than 413.
problem: normalizeError recognizes malformed JSON but not body-parser entity.too.large. A controlled client error becomes an operational alarm.
impact: Security: size limit still works; no payload acceptance or stack leak shown. Business: misleading alerts. Users: incorrect retry guidance. Likelihood: low for ordinary login. Exploitability: simple oversized request.
repro: Send a JSON body over 1 MB to local login; inspect status. See input-probes.mjs.
fix: Map entity.too.large to a safe 413 response and leave unknown errors masked. Apply analogous explicit mappings only where supported by middleware contracts.
test: YES — large body gives 413 without stack; malformed JSON still gives 400; genuine bugs remain 500.

title: Shared office IP is throttled before per-user limits matter

problem: The global 600/15-minute IP budget remains below a single user’s 1,200 budget. Adding a user limiter did not solve shared-office contention.
impact: Security: protective limiter exists. Business/users: ordinary staff share throttling and see failed loads. Likelihood: medium to high in shared offices with polling/tabs. Exploitability: no malicious actor needed. Production: intermittent apparent slowness.

title: Target reporting repeats client-allocation queries per month
evidence: [.qa-audit/production-2026-10-04/final-probes.json](<C:/Users/JARVIS/Desktop/Al Jazeera CRM/.qa-audit/production-2026-10-04/final-probes.json>): warm six-month report, 12 clients: 234 database calls in 316 ms locally (78 deployments.find, 78 mobilisations.find, 72 clientpayments.find, six target reads).
problem: Each month independently computes client payment allocations, including repeated reads of the same client history. Work scales with months times clients.
impact: Security: none demonstrated. Business/users: report latency and database load grow with clients/history. Likelihood: high as usage grows. Exploitability: ordinary report. Production: measured query amplification, not a claimed production response time.
repro: Run scoping-performance.mjs to seed the 12-client fixture, then final-probes.mjs for the warm query count. The initial cold count included model initialization and is not used here.
fix: Load the required clients and financial histories once per request, compute allocations once per client, and reuse across month buckets. Then measure query count and p50/p95 on realistic sanitized data. Avoid a long-lived financial cache until invalidation is defined.
test: YES — totals match existing results for partial/approved payments and date boundaries; query count no longer multiplies full client-history reads by six.

title: API requests have no application timeout
component: Shared Axios client; session refresh and page requests
evidence: [.qa-audit/production-2026-10-04/deep-evidence.json](<C:/Users/JARVIS/Desktop/Al Jazeera CRM/.qa-audit/production-2026-10-04/deep-evidence.json>): source-identical Axios configuration had timeout:0 and remained pending after 1.2 seconds against a deliberately hanging local HTTP server; the test explicitly canceled it.
problem: No finite request timeout bounds an unresponsive connection. Boot refresh and loading states depend on requests completing.
impact: Security: none established. Business/users: indefinite loading when a connection remains open but never responds. Likelihood: medium during infrastructure failures. Exploitability: not required. Production: failure-mode weakness; 1.2 seconds is a test observation, not proof that every slow request hangs forever.
repro: Run deep-tests.mjs hanging-server probe; inspect timeout and pending state. Only Vite constant/base URL setup was adapted for Node.
fix: Set endpoint-appropriate timeouts and cancellation; bound refresh separately; provide retryable errors. Do not automatically retry financial writes without idempotency.
test: YES — hanging refresh exits loading with a recoverable state; slow read times out; canceled/unmounted requests do not update UI; timed-out mutation is not blindly repeated.

title: Release automation has no quality gate, while both repositories fail lint
evidence: [.qa-audit/production-2026-10-04/server-lint.log](<C:/Users/JARVIS/Desktop/Al Jazeera CRM/.qa-audit/production-2026-10-04/server-lint.log>): one error.
